what: Proposed `_OOS_HEADER_RE` is not semantically equivalent to the awk FINDING branch for tag-after-title headers
scenario_or_breakage: Awk uses `index($0,"[OUT_OF_SCOPE]")` anywhere on the line after `^###[[:space:]]+FINDING_[0-9]+:`; Python `FINDING_\d+:\s*\[OUT_OF_SCOPE\]` requires the tag immediately after the colon (whitespace only). Headers like `### FINDING_1: Some Title [OUT_OF_SCOPE]` count in awk but not in Python, so bash and Python gates can disagree on defense-in-depth inputs even though the plan claims lockstep parity
suggested_fix: Only worth fixing if that header shape must be supported: split FINDING detection in Python to `^###\s+FINDING_\d+:` plus `'[OUT_OF_SCOPE]' in line` (mirror awk), or narrow awk to the same anchored tag rule and document the canonical header grammar
